methodology: The study involved compression tests of geometrically identical structural channel sections fabricated from fiber-epoxy composites made with flax, jute, hemp, glass and carbon fibers. The results were compared based on the properties measured in these tests.
research_objective: To compare the structural compression characteristics of natural and synthetic fiber-reinforced epoxy composites (flax, jute, hemp, glass, and carbon) to determine if natural fibers can replace synthetic fibers in existing applications.

key_findings.finding: Natural fiber composites (flax) generally have equivalent or slightly better compression properties compared to glass fiber composites under the same fiber mass.
